items.title: BN ready to include PN in Melaka government if coalition wins
items.summary: TANGGA BATU: Barisan Nasional (BN) is ready to bring Perikatan Nasional (PN) into the Melaka government if the two coalitions win the state election. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said cooperation between the two coalitions should continue beyond the election, including through the formation of a joint state government. "After Nov 14, as BN chairman, if BN and PN are blessed with victory, God willing, the Melaka government will also involve PN in its formation.

items.title: Subsidy leakages: RM82.85mil worth of goods seized in 5,893 cases since 2023
items.summary: Another 1,722 cases involved petrol, with seizures valued at RM5.43 million, while 1,408 cases involved packet cooking oil, with seizures worth RM17.74 million. "For diesel, Sarawak recorded the highest number of cases at 623, with seizures valued at RM22,398,348, followed by Sabah with 363 cases involving RM7,653,887 worth of seizures and Kedah with 308 cases involving RM3,776,130. "For petrol, Kelantan recorded the highest number of cases at 786, with seizures valued at RM351,872.24, followed by Sabah with 629 cases involving RM2,050,806.80 worth of seizures and Perlis with 130 cases involving RM96,263.86.

items.title: Spain hit by nationwide strike over housing crisis ahead of Nov 29 election
items.summary: MADRID: Thousands of Spaniards left their workplaces and hit the streets on Wednesday as a general strike sought to crank up pressure on the key issue of housing weeks before a snap election. Unions reported a "massive" uptake in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, which also aims to up the ante on wages and public services, but business leaders played down the participation. Public rail operator Renfe said 24 per cent of its high-speed services were cancelled, while around 20 per cent of trains were scrapped in the sprawling commuter networks of Madrid and Barcelona.

items.title: Gunmen ambush police convoy in Pakistan, killing eight officers
items.summary: PESHAWAR: Gunmen attacked a police convoy on its way to an illegal gold mining operation in Pakistan's northwestern region on Wednesday, killing eight officers, officials said. A senior administrative official in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province's Kohat district told AFP eight police personnel were killed and 13 others were injured. Militants set two police vehicles on fire during the assault, while two other police vehicles and one private vehicle were missing, the official said.

items.title: Spain investigates alleged child sexual abuse material on TikTok
items.summary: MADRID: Spanish prosecutors on Wednesday ordered an investigation into the alleged distribution of child sexual abuse material on TikTok, following a complaint filed by anti-disinformation group Maldita.es. A prosecutor has been appointed to investigate possible offences involving the production and distribution of child sexual abuse material and the corruption of minors on the social media platform, Spain's public prosecutor's office said in a statement. It follows a complaint submitted to the office's cybercrime unit by Maldita.es, which on Monday accused TikTok of not doing enough to prevent paedophiles from accessing child sexual abuse material or soliciting images from children on the platform.

items.title: 150 Bersatu members quit party ahead of Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA: A total of 150 members of Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) in Hang Tuah Jaya have announced their departure from the party, three days before polling in the Melaka election. Former Bersatu Hang Tuah Jaya deputy division chief Md Firdaus Mashor said the decision was made collectively following discussions and agreement among the leadership and members. Firdaus also resigned as Bersatu Melaka information secretary.

items.title: Zahid confident Negri Sembilan political impasse will be resolved soon
items.summary: TANGGA BATU: The political and administrative impasse in Negri Sembilan is expected to be resolved soon through ongoing discussions involving the relevant parties, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Zahid, who is also Umno president and Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said efforts were underway to find a solution, potentially involving the party's central and state leadership, as well as the Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar. He said the discussions would prioritise the interests of the people, particularly with the state budget due to be tabled soon.

items.title: Meta, TikTok join Google in opposing Indonesia's proposed AI copyright rules
items.summary: JAKARTA: Digital platforms Meta and TikTok joined Google on Wednesday in pushing back against proposed revisions to Indonesia's copyright law that would require digital platforms to pay publishers for displaying news content and set rules for AI. Agung Pamungkas, Google's Indonesia government affairs and public policy manager, told a parliamentary hearing that requiring tech platforms to pay compensation for showing links of news content from publishers would limit Indonesians' access to news. Berni Moestafa, Meta's public policy head in Indonesia, said requiring platforms to pay compensation meant news "publishers could lose readership traffic as well as potential advertising and subscription revenue".

items.title: US midterm results put pro-Israel powerhouse AIPAC on the defensive
items.summary: Candidates of all stripes long courted the American Israel Public Affairs Committee's support. "To Aipac... Officially, Aipac is non-partisan.

items.title: Flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak rise to 1,435
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees in Selangor and Perak rose to 1,435 from 406 families, with nine temporary relief centres operating as of 10pm. The figure was up from 1,359 evacuees from 391 families at eight relief centres recorded at 4.30pm. Perak recorded 302 evacuees from 87 families at two relief centres in Hilir Perak.

items.title: Indonesia's Gibran quits as vice-president amid eligibility controversy
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has resigned, an aide said on Wednesday, a move that threatens to split a key political alliance and risks further political uncertainty in Southeast Asia's largest economy. Gibran, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, has come under intense scrutiny from lawmakers following Constitutional Court and Supreme Court rulings last month that his education documents did not meet election requirements. The aide, Budi Arie Setiadi, told Reuters that Gibran had tendered his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto earlier on Wednesday.

items.title: Missing sailors expose human cost of Iran war at sea
items.summary: Kumar was one of six crew members on two Iran-linked cargo vessels last seen in Iranian waters in May before disappearing. Commercial ships have come under fire since the United States and Israel's war on Iran began on Feb 28. Teheran attacked ships to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz and the US in turn struck Iran-linked ships to impose a blockade on Iranian ports.

items.title: Don't dissolve Parliament over cabinet reshuffle, says Fuziah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parliament should not be dissolved simply because of questions surrounding a cabinet reshuffle when the government remains functional and commands majority support, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh. She said that after nearly four years of the Unity Government, the country should be able to focus on more pressing priorities, including investment, job opportunities, the cost of living and the long-standing institutional reform agenda. "A cabinet reshuffle is part of the process of strengthening the administration.

items.title: Ramanan: Loke's resignation a big loss
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has described Anthony Loke as a principled man, saying his resignation as transport minister was a big loss. Ramanan said any cabinet reshuffle was for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to decide. Loke resigned as transport minister with immediate effect yesterday following the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision allowing Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest.

items.title: Selangor shuts waterfall areas over safety concerns
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: All waterfall recreational areas in permanent forest reserves in Selangor have been closed with immediate effect until further notice due to unpredictable weather conditions. The Selangor Forestry Department said the closure was ordered on safety grounds as changing weather conditions could increase risks to visitors. "The public are prohibited from entering the closed waterfall areas or carrying out any recreational activities at these locations while the closure order remains in force.

items.title: NST Leader: Malaysia's zero-waste ambition needs funding, action and accountability
items.summary: First, urban circularity, which involves recovering, repairing, reusing and recycling materials, can protect supply chains from global disruptions while creating jobs in repair and waste sorting. Second, tracking materials digitally can identify waste chemistry and hold manufacturers accountable under extended producer responsibility laws. While urban waste programmes can secure incentives, underfunded districts may lag behind.

items.title: Policeman seriously injured in parang attack at Kepong apartment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A policeman was seriously injured after being attacked with a sharp weapon by a man at an apartment in Desa Jaya, Kepong, today. The policeman was believed to have been attacked while a team was conducting an operation at one of the apartment units. A video circulating on social media showed a man attacking an individual believed to be a policeman with two parangs.

items.title: Perkeso told to expedite benefits for injured journalists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has directed the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) to expedite benefits for two journalists injured in a road accident in Perak. Speaking at the Perkeso Media Awards 2026 gathering, Ramanan said journalists often worked in difficult conditions to ensure accurate reporting. He said Perkeso would provide the necessary protection to journalists.

items.title: NSTP sweeps top honours at Perkeso Media Awards 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd (NSTP) emerged among the top winners at the Perkeso I Lindung U Media Awards 2026, securing several honours for impactful journalism. In the Best Print Media Report category, Harian Metro journalist Mohd Alhafiz Ithnin clinched first place. The Perkeso I Lindung U Media Awards 2026 recognise media practitioners who consistently deliver accurate information and raise public awareness of the Social Security Organisation's (Perkeso) role in safeguarding people's welfare.

items.title: 400k Malaysia-Singapore commuters to benefit from social security amendment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An amendment that will benefit about 400,000 workers who commute daily between Malaysia and Singapore will be passed before the end of the year, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said. The first amendment is to the Self-Employment Social Security Act 2017 (Act 789). He said the second amendment, to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 (Act 800), concerned the post-maternity leave allowance.

items.title: Ramanan lauds media for taking government policies to millions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has praised journalists for their role in bringing government policies and initiatives to the public. "You play a very important role as the link between the government and the people, delivering information responsibly and ethically," he said at the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) Media Awards 2026 tonight. Ramanan said journalists helped take government announcements far beyond the venues where they were made.

items.title: Pope draws huge crowds at Argentina shrine before Peru homecoming
items.summary: LUJÁN: Pope Leo XIV drew vast crowds to Argentina's holiest shrine Wednesday, the final day of his visit before he departs for Peru, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary. Authorities said two million people packed the streets around the Basilica of Lujan, with some climbing fences, barriers, trees and lampposts for a glimpse of the pontiff as crowds chanted "thank you Leo for your blessing." The stop at Lujan is the emotional centerpiece of Leo's first visit to Argentina, where his predecessor Francis never returned home as pope.

items.title: Malaysian Bar challenges legality of Najib's house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Bar has filed a legal challenge to Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest arrangement, arguing that it is unconstitutional and has no basis in law. The application names the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform), the Prisons Commissioner-General and Najib as respondents. In its accompanying statement, the Bar argued that house arrest did not fall within the meaning of a pardon, reprieve or respite under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: 4 foreigners rob man of RM10k at Penang petrol station
items.summary: Police said the suspects were believed to be from Central Asia. Police are tracking down the two men and two women involved in the robbery. Seberang Prai Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said the incident occurred at 11.30am yesterday at the entrance to a BHPetrol station along Jalan Samagagah.

items.title: RON97 drops 50 sen, unsubsidised RON95 down 40 sen, diesel 25 sen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The retail price of RON97 will drop by 50 sen per litre, while unsubsidised RON95 will fall by 40 sen and unsubsidised diesel by 25 sen, effective tomorrow until Nov 18. The new prices are RM4.20 per litre for RON97, RM3.87 for RON95 and RM4.87 for diesel. "The subsidised petroleum prices remain unchanged, with RON95 under Budi95 at RM1.99 per litre; diesel under Budi Diesel at RM2.10 per litre; the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) at RM2.05 per litre; and the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) at RM2.15 per litre.

items.title: Sabah hospital separates conjoined twins in second successful surgery
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah has successfully performed its second separation surgery on conjoined twins, bringing forward the operation after one of the babies required increasing respiratory support. They underwent the complex procedure at Sabah Women and Children's Hospital in Likas. The operation required close coordination among multidisciplinary teams from Sabah Women and Children's Hospital, Hospital Tunku Azizah in Kuala Lumpur and Hospital Umum Sarawak.

items.title: Malaysians arrested in Mauritius over RM9mil cannabis haul knew they carried drugs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three Malaysians arrested in Mauritius with 76.14kg of cannabis worth RM9.87 million knowingly transported the drugs after collecting them in Bangkok, police said. Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the trio, comprising a couple and another individual recruited through a holiday package, knew they were carrying drugs. He said investigations had established that the suspects travelled from Malaysia to Bangkok, where they collected the drugs before continuing their journey to Mauritius.

items.title: Najib's daughter conveys his message to Melaka voters ahead of polls
items.summary: MELAKA: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's daughter, Nooryana Najwa, better known as Yana Najib, said her father had a message for the people of Melaka ahead of the 16th Melaka state election. She said her father wanted to remind voters that Barisan Nasional was the coalition best placed to secure their future, particularly that of the younger generation. "Datuk Seri Najib has always hoped for a BN victory.

items.title: NCID seeks 1,000 more personnel to target drug syndicates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) is seeking 1,000 additional positions to strengthen intelligence and enforcement operations against major drug syndicates amid manpower shortages. He said the additional manpower would strengthen the department's Intelligence and Operations Division, whose undercover operatives gathered intelligence, identified syndicate networks and supported major enforcement operations. We would only be arresting drug addicts or street-level pushers," he said.

items.title: Melaka polls: Najib's house arrest should not be election campaign material
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has reminded all parties against using the issue of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest as campaign material in the Melaka election. "Granting a pardon is the absolute prerogative of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and the Malay Rulers. "The matter is enshrined in the Federal Constitution.

items.title: Cabinet to be briefed on latest constitutional amendments separating AG, Public Prosecutor roles
items.summary: The meeting was chaired by Pengerang Member of Parliament, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Also present were Parit Sulong MP and Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, William Leong Jee Keen (Selayang), Syahredzan Johan (Bangi), Ramkarpal Singh (Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (Beluran), Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (Kota Bharu) and Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muar). Larut MP and Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin, Alor Gajah MP and Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Datuk Lo Su Fui (Tawau) and Roy Angau Gingkoi (Lubok Antu) were unable to attend the meeting due to unavoidable circumstances.

items.title: Anwar, Wan Azizah convey condolences over Melaka PKR leader J. Samivel’s passing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail have extended their condolences to the family of Alor Gajah PKR branch vice-chief J. Samivel, who died in a road accident in Jasin earlier today. Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, said in a Facebook post today that Samivel, 62, was also the representative for P. Denesh, the PH candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka state election. Jasin police chief Supt Lee Robert said police received a report about the accident involving the car Samivel was travelling in at Jalan Pondok Batang, Jasin, at about 12.45 pm today.

items.title: Nine-year-old boy killed in suspected crocodile attack in Kudat
items.summary: KUDAT, Nov 11 — A nine-year-old boy was killed in a suspected crocodile attack while trying to retrieve a fishing hook caught in Sungai Semayan, Kampung Semayan, Pulau Banggi, today. The victim, identified as Mohamad Hilmi Nurjahid, was a Year Three pupil of Sekolah Kebangsaan Semayan. Kudat District Police Chief Supt Mohd Haris Ibrahim said the incident occurred at about 3.30pm while the boy was fishing with his elder brother.

items.title: Anwar hails Malaysia’s leap to 27th globally in digital, AI competitiveness
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Malaysia has climbed seven rungs to 27th place out of 70 economies in the IMD World Digital and AI Ranking (WDAIR) 2026 from 34th place last year, becoming the second-highest-ranked country in ASEAN after Singapore. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the achievement was driven particularly by a 21-place improvement in artificial intelligence (AI) adoption to 14th place globally, a 10-place improvement in efficiency to 28th place, and Malaysia’s implementation of the national AI strategy, which ranked 12th. “Malaysia also ranks 18th in workforce development, second globally in graduates in sciences, fifth in venture capital, sixth in high-tech exports and eighth in investment incentives for AI.

items.title: Stay away from 14 Hulu Selangor rivers, waterfalls amid water surge danger, Fire Dept warns; Pertak, Siling, Batang Kali top hotspots
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR, Nov 11 — Fourteen recreational areas in Hulu Selangor have been identified as high-risk locations for water surges, with Sungai Pertak, Sungai Siling and Sungai Batang Kali emerging as the three main hotspots. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said Sungai Batang Kali recorded four water surge incidents this year, followed by Sungai Siling with three and Sungai Pertak with two. He said the other 11 high-risk locations were Lata Medang in Kuala Kubu Bharu, Sungai Inki in Kalumpang, River View Sungai Bernam in Hulu Selangor, Sungai Sendat and Sungai Tua in Ulu Yam, Sungai Kedondong in Batang Kali, Sungai Cilin in Kuala Kubu Bharu, Sungai Pinang in Batang Kali, Air Terjun Serendah in Serendah, Air Terjun Semangkuk and Sungai Liam in Hulu Selangor.

items.title: IGP says Prisons Dept responsible for Najib’s home security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Prisons Department is fully responsible for the security arrangements for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, who has been serving the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta here since yesterday. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), as a law enforcement agency, maintained close cooperation with the Prisons Department to ensure compliance with the security requirements. Mohd Khalid said PDRM had assigned several officers to assist the Prisons Department throughout the former prime minister’s period of serving the remainder of his sentence at home.

items.title: Government steps in with RM15m monthly subsidy as palm oil costs rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government has approved a special incentive of about RM15 million a month under the Cooking Oil Price Control Mechanism (MKHMM) to maintain ceiling prices and ensure a stable supply of bottled pure palm cooking oil. Armizan said the sustained increase in global CPO prices since June 2025 had placed mounting cost pressures on manufacturers, prompting some companies to halt production of bottled cooking oil. Meanwhile, PRESMA president Datuk Mohammed Mosin Abdul Razak said stable cooking oil prices would help restaurant operators better manage their business costs.

items.title: Car washer charged with murder over fatal Jalan Kuching crash that killed lorry driver
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A car washer was brought before the Magistrate’s Court today on a charge of murdering a lorry driver in a fatal accident on Jalan Kuching here earlier this month. He is accused of killing Indonesian lorry driver Yudi Hartono, 39, on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut at 4.44am on November 4. Meanwhile, in a statement today, Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said that preliminary investigations found the car driven by the accused, with a 46-year-old male passenger, had struck the rear right side of the lorry.

items.title: Azalina: Land acquisition must uphold rule of law, respect constitutional safeguards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Challenging decisions involving compulsory land acquisition is not an act of disloyalty but an essential part of upholding the rule of law, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said that as Malaysia continued to pursue economic growth and modernise its infrastructure, compulsory land acquisition remained a necessary but sensitive public duty requiring transparency, procedural fairness and adequate compensation. “From the perspective of democracy, challenging the exercise of power is not an act of disloyalty, rather it’s an essential part of the rule of law,” she said at the “Challenging Land Acquisition in Malaysia” book launch here today.

items.title: Nadma deploys 102,000 personnel ahead of 2026/2027 northeast monsoon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) has mobilised nearly 102,000 personnel from various departments and agencies, along with 40,000 operational assets, in preparation for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL). Nadma Deputy Director of Operations Datuk Dr Abdul Gapar Abu Bakar said the preparations also included 8,321 temporary relief centres nationwide, with a combined capacity of up to 1.9 million flood victims. Commenting on ground-level operational coordination, Abdul Gapar said district officers are responsible for mobilising initial flood response by activating the District Disaster Operations Control Centre.

items.title: Re-ignite the Malaysian Dream, Lim Kit Siang urges Melaka voters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Veteran DAP leader Lim Kit Siang today called on voters in Melaka to “re-ignite the Malaysian Dream”, describing Transport Minister Anthony Loke's resignation as a starting point for renewed efforts to build a united and world-class Malaysia. Lim traced the roots of the “Malaysian Dream” to before independence, citing Chinese educationist Lim Lian Geok's 1956 message to Utusan Melayu on the need to cultivate a Malaysian mindset. Nevertheless, Lim urged Malaysians not to abandon the aspirations of the Malaysian Dream.

items.title: Flood situation worsens in Selangor as evacuees increase, improves in Perak
items.summary: In Selangor, the number of flood evacuees at five PPS in Kuala Selangor increased to 1,032 people, from 289 families, compared with 945 people from 265 families this morning. According to the Social Welfare Department's (JKM) InfoBencana portal, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela housed the highest number of evacuees, at 416, followed by Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (287), SK Parit Mahang (238), Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (77) and SK Jaya Setia (12). In Perak, the number of flood evacuees in Hilir Perak district decreased to 330 people, from 94 families, compared with 380 people, from 108 families, this morning.

items.title: Tragedy on the Melaka campaign trail: Car hits lorry, Alor Gajah PKR deputy chief dies in crash outside campaign operations room
items.summary: JASIN, Nov 11 — An aide of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka election was killed today when the car he was driving collided with a lorry, three days to voting day. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, paid tribute to J. Samivel, 62, in a Facebook post today, noting that the deceased was also Alor Gajah PKR deputy division chief. Brother Samivel, the representative of the Harapan candidate for the Asahan state seat, was killed in a road accident this afternoon.

items.title: Funding Malaysia’s SMEs is about quality and not quantity, says economy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government wants to improve the quality of financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to strengthen local firms’ global competitiveness and enable workers to earn higher wages and hold better-quality jobs. Although Malaysia had recorded encouraging economic growth, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today that structural challenges still needed to be addressed so that SMEs could expand and improve productivity. “Particularly in ensuring productivity improvements that can eventually translate into higher wages and quality employment,” he told reporters after the launch of the World Bank’s 33rd Malaysia Economic Monitor, titled ‘From Quantity to Quality: Financing Malaysia’s Productive SMEs’, here today.

items.title: Kelantan exco shake-up: Deputy MB says Bersatu rep’s appointment not renewed, with Sultan’s consent
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 11 — Ayer Lanas assemblyman Datuk Kamarudin Md Nor’s appointment as a Kelantan state executive council (exco) member was not renewed, effective November 9. Kelantan Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the decision had received the consent of the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V. He said the two portfolios previously held by Kamarudin would be redistributed to two existing exco members to ensure the smooth running of state administration. Kamarudin previously oversaw the Tourism, Culture, Arts and Heritage portfolio.

items.title: Skudai Deepavali fireworks stunt ends in court for four, one just 16
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 11 — Four men, including a secondary school student, claimed trial at the Magistrate’s Court here today to charges of setting off fireworks on a main road during Deepavali last Sunday. The accused – P. Ruban, 20; S. Tharun, 18; H. Periuthiv, 19; and a 16-year-old – entered their pleas after the charges were read to them separately. The incident allegedly took place at 1.30am last Sunday on Jalan Skudai-Gelang Patah, near the Taman Nesa traffic lights junction in Skudai.

items.title: Anwar: ‘Hundreds of years of service’ no excuse, corrupt people belong in prison
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said that even hundreds of years of service cannot justify letting anyone plunder the wealth of the people and the country. He added that those who commit corruption belong in prison. “Even hundreds of years of service cannot be a reason for us to let anyone plunder and rob the wealth of the people and the country.

items.title: What are the terms of Najib’s house arrest? Saifuddin Nasution to explain in Dewan Rakyat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he will address the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow to lay out the operational conditions and custodial restrictions governing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s transition into house arrest. The upcoming parliamentary briefing follows Najib’s arrival at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence in Kuala Lumpur at 9.27pm yesterday to begin serving the remainder of his six-year SRC International sentence at home. His release from prison walls was finalised after High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin set aside a contentious November 6 discharge order and replaced it in full, explicitly authorizing Najib to serve his custodial sentence at his private home until August 23, 2028.

items.title: Monsoon surge triggers continuous rain alert for Kelantan, Terengganu and Sabah until tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 – The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MET Malaysia) has issued an updated continuous rain alert for parts of Kelantan, Terengganu, and Sabah, as an incoming monsoon surge threatens to trigger persistent downpours through tomorrow. In an advisory released at 2.00pm today, the department explained that atmospheric simulation models indicate a monsoon surge is entering regional airspace, creating unstable weather conditions likely to dump sustained, heavy precipitation along the eastern seaboard of Peninsular Malaysia and eastern Sabah over the next 24 hours. In neighbouring Terengganu, the warning encompasses the northern and coastal districts of Besut, Setiu, Kuala Terengganu, and Kuala Nerus.

items.title: Loke: JPJ’s war on overloaded lorries must continue even without me, as it involves human lives
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — In his parting words to the Transport Ministry, Anthony Loke today urged the Road Transport Department to continue its “war” against overloading in commercial vehicles even after he leaves as transport minister. Loke, who effectively resigned as transport minister yesterday, said there would be people cheering that the minister who refused to compromise on overloading, and who they felt interfered with their livelihood, was gone. “‘The minister has left, we can overload again like in the past, no problem,’” he said in his 48-minute speech at the Transport Ministry here, describing how overloaders would feel.

items.title: Umno says opposing Najib’s house arrest could amount to challenging King’s constitutional powers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Umno has warned that actions perceived as protests against the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, including the house arrest provision, could be construed as challenging the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s constitutional authority. In a media statement posted on his Facebook page, Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the party believed the conditional pardon granted under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution reflected the King’s constitutional powers and rights, which must be respected by all institutions and the public. The party said any action taken in protest, including using the conditional pardon decree as justification, could be seen as an act of defiance against the King’s constitutional authority.

items.title: Rosmah not allowed to live with Najib during house arrest, Umno leader says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s family members and other individuals are not permitted to live with him while he serves the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, according to Umno Women’s executive council member Datuk Nurulhidayah Ahmad Zahid. Nurulhidayah said Najib’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, is expected to stay at her residence in Pavilion instead of the Taman Duta house where he is serving his sentence, Harian Metro reported today. Responding to questions on Threads about the implementation of the house arrest order, Nurulhidayah said the Jalan Langgak Duta residence had been gazetted as a prison, meaning standard prison rules would apply.

items.title: ‘Camera must follow the schedule’: Hannah Yeoh says as DBKL makes body cams compulsory for field operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will equip its enforcement unit with 200 additional body-worn cameras, bringing its total number of devices to 305. Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh and Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud announced the expansion at DBKL’s 57th Enforcement Day parade in Bandar Tun Razak today. Fadlun said the additional cameras were part of DBKL’s efforts to modernise enforcement operations, with footage providing a record of officers’ actions in the event of complaints or disputes.

items.title: BN MPs want AG to take leave over four-day delay in Najib’s house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Several Barisan Nasional (BN) MPs today called for the Attorney General (AG) to be placed on temporary leave pending an independent investigation into the delay in implementing Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest. Manndzri said Najib’s continued detention at Kajang Prison for four more days could amount to unlawful detention, particularly as no court order had been obtained to justify the delay. Najib was transferred from Kajang Prison to his residence last night to serve the remainder of his six-year SRC International prison sentence under house arrest, following a fresh High Court order.

items.title: MCMC finds 23 internet quality breaches in Muar, takes action against telcos
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has issued eight non-compliance notices to telecommunications companies after an audit this year uncovered 23 breaches of internet service quality standards at 16 locations in the Muar parliamentary constituency. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the audit, conducted on six service providers between Jan 1 and Oct 1, found that only 18 of the 34 locations assessed in Muar met the Mandatory Standards for Quality of Service (MSQoS). Syed Saddiq had wanted to know the measures to address poor internet service quality and limited connectivity in parts of Muar, despite data from the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) showing 100 per cent coverage in Parit Amat, Sungai Kelat, Tanjung Tohor and Sungai Muda.

items.title: DAP yet to pick candidate to replace Loke as transport minister, for PM to decide
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — Anthony Loke today confirmed that DAP has yet to discuss a candidate to replace him as transport minister, a post he resigned from with immediate effect yesterday. Asked by reporters at the Transport Ministry here whether DAP had discussed a potential successor, Loke gave a brief “not yet” response. “This is the prime minister's jurisdiction, discuss with him,” he replied when asked whether or not the decision would be left to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Ex-Tabung Haji chief Azeez gets court nod to challenge IRB’s cancellation of RM4.8m tax deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim today secured High Court permission to challenge the Inland Revenue Board’s (IRB) decision to revoke a RM4.8 million tax settlement he says he had fully paid. The court today allowed his application for leave to commence judicial review, paving the way for a full hearing on whether IRB was legally entitled to cancel the agreement. The dispute centres on a settlement agreement signed on February 9, 2022, covering Azeez’s tax and penalties for the assessment years 2011 to 2020.

items.title: Trader suspected of sourcing frozen chicken from Thailand arrested in raid
items.summary: -KOTA BHARU, Nov 11 — A frozen chicken trader in Pasir Tumboh, here, is suspected of obtaining between 300 and 500 boxes of stock from a supplier in Thailand before selling them at his wholesale premises. General Operations Force (GOF) Southeast Brigade Commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the matter came to light following the arrest of a 38-year-old man during an Op Salju Mega raid at a premises along Jalan Pasir Puteh, Kampung Pasir Tumboh, at about noon yesterday. “An inspection by the enforcement team uncovered 209 boxes of frozen chicken, weighing 2,508 kilogrammes and worth RM42,845, stored in a refrigerated container at the premises,” he said in a statement last night.

items.title: Social media firms face Dec 28 deadline under Online Safety Act
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Licensed social media service providers must submit their Online Safety Plans to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) by Dec 28 at the latest, in compliance with the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866). She said social media platforms were also expected to implement user age verification requirements in early January 2027, following the end of the current transition period. Teo said MCMC had issued directives to social media service providers, including Meta, TikTok and Google, to ensure the implementation of age verification mechanisms.

items.title: ‘A leader must be decisive’: Loke says ‘conscience is clear’ as he reflects on time as minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — Anthony Loke today said his conscience is clear as he had done his best during his nearly four years as transport minister, while reaffirming that his resignation took effect yesterday following the court order allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve his sentence under house arrest. Speaking at the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly and Deepavali celebrations today, Loke thanked everyone in the ministry and apologised to anyone who may have been affected by his words, actions or past mistakes. Loke said civil servants were “most worried and disliked it the most when a minister sits on a decision, sits on files, not making decisions”.
